items.title: Alice Zeno Interview, 1958-12-10
items.q: You see I had lost already three children before I raised George.

ctx.x: Well I can't complain. No that's a good name. It's easy to remember. It's easier to remember and say it that way.

You see I had lost already three children before I raised George. And I was so outdone, so discouraged. I was losing my mind. So when George came, my mother said, Peleli George, he live. I said, well that's, we called him George. But he wasn't christened George.
Did he practice much around the house? Was he always bothering you playing a lot?

items.title: George Lewis Interview, 1958-11-14
items.q: I worked for one job, I was just talking to my mother right there.

ctx.x: I worked for one job, I was just talking to my mother right there. Decatur, not my son, he's bringing me over here. Decatur, Toulouse, Decatur. And then there's a little Shaw Street coming from St. Peter. Wilkinson. Wilkinson. They had a saloon right on that corner. And I worked there one night from eight until four in the morning for six bits.
Which corner was it? Downtown or the uptown?

items.title: Alice Zeno Interview, 1960-01-25
items.q: Never thought I would raise George. to the age that he is now.

ctx.x: Y'all was the only child he would raise.
The only best left. And I didn't think I would raise him. Never thought I would raise George. to the age that he is now. Well, God knows all. He knows best.
I was wondering about any of the other dances,
